title: Cross-stitch bumblebee on Aida
subtitle: A cheerful bumblebee in yellow, black and white on 14-count ivory Aida
excerpt: This bumblebee design uses yellow, black, white and pale grey to render a garden bumblebee in approximately 50 by 40 stitches, finishing at around 9 by 7 cm on 14-count ivory Aida. The wings use a single strand of grey back-stitch to give a translucent, gauzy appearance.
sourceNotes: Original design. The buff-tailed bumblebee (Bombus terrestris) is the most common British garden bumblebee; colour pattern from RSPB field reference.

glossaryTerms.definition: A small raised knot formed by wrapping the thread around the needle one or more times before inserting the needle back into the fabric. Used in cross-stitch for eyes, flower centres, and small textural details.

Stitch the yellow body segments first.
Begin with the two yellow bands using DMC 972 and two strands. Fill each band in horizontal rows. Leave the black stripes as gaps between the yellow fills.

Work the head, black body stripes, and abdomen tip in DMC 310. The thorax (back section between the wings) is worked in a mix of 310 and white fuzzy texture. Work black first, then add small white stitches over the top if the chart calls for them.
Add the white buff tail and wing roots.
The base of the abdomen uses 3865 in two strands. Work the fluffy thorax collar in short back-stitches of white to give texture.
Outline the wings in single-strand back-stitch.
Using one strand of DMC 648, outline the wing shape in back-stitch. The interior of each wing remains unstitched; the ivory background shows through to suggest translucency.
Work the eye as a French knot in 310. Stitch the antennae in back-stitch with a small dot at each tip.
Trim to a 4 cm border and mount in a 10 cm round hoop for display, or frame in a small 12 × 12 cm square mount. The ivory background works well behind the open wing design.
